home_title: Explore how languages share, differ, and change.
home_subtitle: Language Patterns documents recurring strategies, pathways, and cycles across the world's languages — from how unrelated languages express “there is” to how negation rebuilds itself over centuries.

section_geographic_distribution_hint: Each dot is one attested language, coloured by the strategy it uses. Click a dot for the surface form.
section_shared_predicates_hint: Many languages use one predicate for more than one of these three. Each language sits in the region covering everything its predicate can express.
section_column_clusters_hint: Two columns count as close when the same language uses one word for both. Branches joining further right are the pairs more languages merge; the column order in the grid and on the map follows this tree, so neighbours behave alike.

section_geographic_distribution_hint_set: Each marker is one attested language, coloured by its evidence set; open it for the expression recorded there.

atlas_subtitle: Every topic on one map. Pick a pattern or pathway to colour languages by strategy or evidence set, or view all topics at once. In the combined view, marker size shows how many topics attest a language.
tags_subtitle: Tags fall into three facets: the meaning at issue, the machinery that carries it, and the process behind it.
contribute_lede: Every row on this site is a claim about a language, and any of it can be wrong. Publishing something does not settle it. Reports go in the issue tracker, fixes go in as pull requests, and both are public from the moment they are filed.
contribute_report_body: A form no speaker would use, a gloss that misreads the morphology, a date taken from an edition the field has moved past, a table row that flattens variation. Naming the language and the problem is enough to file; the forms ask for more only where it helps.
contribute_fix_body: Each entry is one TypeScript file named after its slug, so /patterns/existence is src/lib/data/patterns/existence.ts. Every entry page links to the file it was rendered from, and editing on GitHub opens a pull request without cloning anything.
contribute_propose_body: An entry starts as a question that several unrelated languages answer in a handful of ways. Two to six recurring answers, with a language or two under each, is enough to open one.
contribute_needs_body: Something a reader can go and check. A grammar, a dictionary, a corpus hit, a wiki page, a thread, a recorded talk, and your own judgement as a speaker all count as evidence, and every kind of it gets named. Speaker judgement stays recorded as speaker judgement, with the variety and the date, instead of being folded into somebody else's citation.
contribute_grades_body: Each attestation carries high, medium, or low. High means a description or a speaker states it directly. Medium means the sources hedge, or one row is standing in for variation. Low means it is inferred or contested. A report that a claim is graded too high is as welcome as a report that it is wrong.
contribute_license_body: Content is under CC BY-SA 4.0, and contributions are taken under the same licence. Contributors keep authorship of what they write, and the file history records who added which claim.
contribute_entry_body: Any of this can be wrong. Dispute what the page says, add a language it is missing, or edit the file it was rendered from.
